text:
lena: quick follow-up from the sync: proposing a lightweight 'broker-proxy' (LPB) as an alternative to keeping a persistent per-tenant sidecar. LPB does capability negotiation + short-lived auth handoff and then either proxies or establishes a tunneled stream to the chosen runtime. want quick takes on security, perf, and rollout.

dan: sounds promising. question: multitenant broker surface = bigger blast radius. do we plan AZ-local LPBs or global?

lena: plan is AZ-local per-region autoscaled pools. each LPB instance is stateless except for ephemeral lease entries in a control-plane cache. tenancy isolation is enforced at runtime and by infra network policies; LPB won't persist secrets.

priya: how do we avoid adding burden to private customers who run their own control planes? we can't force them to run LPB. manifest should be opt-in.

lena: agree. add an optional manifest field under runtime.handoff so private deployments ignore LPB by default.

hugo: uptime/latency: LPB adds a hop. propose two modes: "audit-proxy" (full proxy, useful for debug/inspection) and "fast-tunnel" (negotiate, then proxy at TCP level). default to fast-tunnel for low-latency routes.

maria: +1. also need billing attribution even when tunneling. handshake should include attribution tags so billing can be computed at runtime.

priya: manifest draft (optional):

```json
{"service":"inference","model":"redwood-xl-6b","runtime":{
  "handoff":{
    "prefer":["lpb","direct"],
    "max_ttl_seconds":180,
    "billing_tag":"hosted:default"
  }
}}
```

priya: note: consumers can omit runtime.handoff entirely for private-only installs.

dan: security controls: LPB -> runtime must use mTLS. LPB issues ephemeral access tokens w/ very short TTLs and proof-of-possession. also add token-replay detection + telemetry.

hugo: failure scenarios: if LPB is degraded, client SDK should be able to fall back to direct runtime URL if tenant has pinned runtime. for hosted customers without pinned runtime, control-plane should provide an alternate hosted proxy or degrade to a cheaper model variant.

lena: agreed. fallback plan: (1) client pin -> direct, (2) control-plane proxy, (3) LPB mediator. we'll add circuit-breakers at LPB to short-circuit to model variants under pressure.

maria: testing matrix I'll run: latency comparison (no LPB vs tunnel vs proxy), failover correctness (LPB down -> client fallback), auth rotation mid-stream, billing attribution accuracy. I'll own harness and metrics.

priya: ops rollout: canary LPB per-region + tenant opt-in flag. we need a per-tenant opt-out for PLG customers too. also include an emergency kill switch that flips feature-flag globally.

infra-bot: infra checklist created: https://infra/repo/LPB/PR-523 7 items incl. mTLS lifecycle, canary config, feature-flag gate, observability dashboards.

dan: naming nit: "LPB" vs "broker" vs "light-proxy". prefer avoiding the ambiguous word "broker" in docs. maybe call it "hand-off-proxy" (HOP)? branding aside, specs look good.

lena: HOP is a good candidate. will pick final name in RFC. next steps: I'll draft an RFC with sequence diagrams for both modes (proxy/tunnel), manifest extension, security model, and canary plan. please add concerns here if anything missing.

hugo: add SLO/latency budget numbers in RFC and specify when to prefer tunnel vs proxy for different endpoints (e.g., streaming vs sync).

priya: add migration notes for private customers who run older control planes (compat shim). they should be able to opt into HOP with zero config if they want.

maria: and include a test that verifies no long-lived secrets are stored on HOP nodes — audit proof.

lena: thanks all 680 4aa. I'll post the RFC link when ready and mark a 2-week review window.
